best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
As we reach August 2026, Broadway shows that premiered in 2020 continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike, representing a particularly significant year in theater history. Despite the unprecedented challenges that marked that season, the productions that made it to opening night showcase remarkable artistic ambition and enduring relevance.

Leading the critical rankings is "A Soldier's Play," Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally received its long-awaited Broadway debut. Critics consistently praise the production's powerful examination of race and justice within a World War II military setting, noting how its themes remain strikingly relevant more than four decades after the play was written. The stellar ensemble cast brings new urgency to Fuller's incisive text.

Ivo van Hove's reimagining of "West Side Story" stands as one of the year's most provocative productions, sharply dividing critical opinion with its radical approach to the beloved musical. Those who champion the production celebrate its bold directorial vision and striking use of video design, while skeptics question whether the experimental staging serves or obscures the material's emotional core.

On the comedic side, "Grand Horizons" offers audiences Bess Wohl's Neil Simon-influenced take on late-life divorce, anchored by performances from Broadway veterans that critics find both poignant and genuinely funny. Meanwhile, Laura Linney's solo turn in "My Name is Lucy Barton" demonstrates the power of intimate storytelling, even as reviewers debate whether Elizabeth Strout's novel fully translates to the stage format.

With an average critical score of 74 out of 100, these productions from 2020 represent a diverse theatrical landscape. Browse the top-rated shows below to find your next Broadway experience.

The highest-rated productions from 2021 span an unusually wide theatrical spectrum.
